title: Kamlesh Chandra Tiwari v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Misra, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; poultry farm not entitled to agricultural tariff.
headnote: A poultry-farm consumer billed in LMV-2 (non-domestic) cannot obtain agricultural or non-commercial rates by importing the U.P. Revenue Code, 2006 definition of 'agriculture'. The U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 classifies consumers into specified categories and has no general agricultural-supply category other than LMV-5 (private tube well/pumping set for irrigation) and HV-4 (lift irrigation). Poultry farming is otherwise a commercial activity. Writ dismissed.
facts: The petitioner held an LMV-2 (non-domestic) electricity connection for a poultry farm. He sought a writ directing the distribution licensee to recast his bills at agricultural or non-commercial rates, because the U.P. Revenue Code, 2006 includes poultry farming in 'agriculture'. The licensee maintained that the Supply Code 2005 has no general agricultural category beyond LMV-5 (irrigation tube well/pumping set) and HV-4 (lift irrigation), and that poultry farming is a commercial activity. The Division Bench heard the State and the licensee.

reusable_constructions.construction: The definition of 'agriculture' in the U.P. Revenue Code, 2006 does not travel into the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 so as to confer agricultural or non-commercial electricity rates on a poultry farm.

The Supply Code 2005 contains no general agricultural-supply category other than LMV-5 (private tube well/pumping set for irrigation) and HV-4 (lift irrigation); a poultry farm, being a commercial activity, is properly billed in LMV-2 (non-domestic).

holding_units.holding: Where the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 classifies consumers into specified categories and contains no general agricultural-supply category other than LMV-5 (private tube well/pumping set for irrigation) and HV-4 (lift irrigation), a poultry-farm consumer billed in LMV-2 (non-domestic light, fan and power) cannot obtain agricultural or non-commercial rates by invoking the U.P. Revenue Code, 2006 definition of 'agriculture', which includes poultry farming; running a poultry farm is otherwise a commercial activity, and the writ seeking recasting of the bill is dismissed.

principle_tags.application: The Court refused to recast LMV-2 poultry-farm billing as agricultural supply by importing the Revenue Code definition of agriculture, holding that the Supply Code's specified categories (LMV-5 and HV-4 for irrigation only) control the rate.
